name: PT Greenwood Sejahtera Tbk

frontmatter.title: GWSA — Value enclosed, catalyst absent
frontmatter.summary: GWSA carries IDR2,225.9bn of investment properties and IDR3,272.0bn of equity-accounted associates, offset by the IDR136.4bn related-party payable that turns reported net cash into net debt. At the observed 86% discount to NAV the stock is fairly priced; we initiate at HOLD with a Rp120 target, implying a -5.1% total return.
thesis: The core is a land bank at major Jakarta arteries, with TCC Batavia, Senayan City, Kuningan City, The Peak Apartment, Lindeteves Trade Center, Emporium Pluit, Holiday Inn Express Pluit and Festival Citylink developments [S2].
Financial rebalancing is largely done — bank liabilities fell from IDR537.6bn to IDR61.9bn, but the IDR136.4bn related-party payable to associates is a senior claim on that cash [S2,S4].

The operating line is structurally loss-making at EBIT and value reaches shareholders only through a sale or distribution; the stock has traded at 86% below NAV for five years and no catalyst to narrow that discount exists today [S2,S0].

catalysts.event: Another round of associate dividends (FY2025 receipts {{fact.F10|money}})

blocks.text: Initiation with a **HOLD** rating and a Rp120 target, implying a -5.1% total return from the last traded price of Rp127. The assets are real and marked conservatively: IDR3,272.0bn of equity‑method associates, IDR2,225.9bn of appraised investment property, IDR1,463.5bn plus IDR294.1bn of current and non‑current real‑estate inventory and IDR147.1bn of hotel and office fixed assets [S2,S5], against a market capitalisation of IDR990.7bn [S0]. What the price also reflects, correctly, is a controlling stake held by two private vehicles (56.2% plus 23.2%), a IDR136.4bn related‑party payable to associates that turns reported net cash into net debt [S4], and five years without a dividend. We therefore carry the observed 86% discount rather than assuming it narrows, which puts fair value close to the price. The operating business is structurally loss‑making at EBIT because overhead is 1.2× revenue [S5]; value comes from the balance sheet, but it reaches minorities only through a sale or a distribution. We would turn positive on a dated distribution, buyback or partial stake sale; absent that, the stock is fairly priced.

PT Greenwood Sejahtera Tbk (GWSA) is a Jakarta‑based property company that owns, develops and operates a portfolio of office towers, shopping malls, apartments and hotels through direct ownership and equity‑accounted associates [S2]. The company’s principal assets are the TCC Batavia complex (a super‑block featuring an office tower, a shopping centre and a hotel), The Peak Apartment (a high‑rise residential tower), and equity stakes in Senayan City, Kuningan City, Festival Citylink, Lindeteves Trade Center and Pluit Propertindo [S2]. Development began with the TCC Batavia project in 2008; the company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in December 2011 [S2].

The Indonesian property sector has historically been dominated by conglomerates that combine development, mall operation and hospitality, often using listed vehicles as holding companies for land banks and completed projects. Greenwood’s model—holding large parcels of inner‑city land while partnering with experienced operators for retail and hotel segments—is common among mid‑size developers in Jakarta.

The **business model** separates three segments: (i) hotel operations (the Holiday Inn Express Pluit), (ii) office leasing (TCC Batavia Tower One), and (iii) apartment sales (The Peak Apartment). The hotel segment contributed IDR56.5bn of revenue in FY2025 and a segment result of IDR23.7bn, while the office segment earned IDR9.9bn and the apartment segment IDR9.8bn [S2]. The consolidated P&L shows a structurally negative EBIT (IDR-60.6bn in FY2025) because operating expense alone was IDR94.7bn on revenue of IDR76.2bn [S5]. The company offsets this operating loss with income from its associates (IDR204.7bn in FY2025) and occasional revaluation gains on investment properties.

The **strategy** is to hold and monetise its land bank through joint‑venture development with operational partners, a model that minimises capital outlay and captures value through equity‑accounted earnings [S2]. Management seeks to “enhance investment, occupancy rates and repeat visits” across the portfolio [S2]. The **geographic footprint** is concentrated in Jakarta’s CBD and North Jakarta, with the TCC Batavia complex located at Jl. K.H. Mas Mansyur and the Holiday Inn Express in Pluit [S2].

**Market position** is that of a niche land‑owner/developer rather than a retail or hospitality operator. The company’s super‑block stakes place it alongside large‑capitalisation property names, but its own revenue base is tiny—the consolidated sales of IDR76.2bn compare with the tens of trillions typical of major listed developers [S2]. The group employed 89 people at the last annual report, which underlines how thin the operating structure is relative to the asset base [S0].

**Segment economics**: the hotel segment (Holiday Inn Express Pluit) is the largest contributor, at IDR56.5bn of revenue and IDR23.7bn of segment result in FY2025, against IDR9.9bn for office leasing and IDR9.8bn for apartment sales [S2]. Two thirds of revenue therefore comes from a single mid‑scale hotel whose building sits inside the investment‑property pool, which is why operating earnings tell us little about what the assets are worth and why we value the balance sheet rather than the P&L.

**The associate portfolio** is the other half of the story. The equity‑method stakes are Senayan City, Kuningan City, Emporium Pluit Mall, Festival Citylink in Bandung and Lindeteves Trade Center [S4]. They earned IDR204.7bn of equity income in FY2025 but paid only IDR98.8bn of dividends to the group, down from IDR341.2bn in FY2024 [S2]: the malls are profitable but their cash is being retained inside the associate vehicles.

**Controlling shareholder and group structure**: PT Prima Permata Sejahtera (56.2%) and PT Kencana Graha Nusamandiri (23.2%) are the principal and controlling shareholders; the ultimate beneficial owners are Erawaty S.G, Harry Gunawan, Eddy Hartono and Ang Andri Pribadi [S2]. Several directors and commissioners have affiliations with PT Kencana Graha Nusamandiri, the controlling shareholder, but the board includes independent commissioners [S2].

The Indonesian property sector is recovering from pandemic‑induced softness, with retail sales and hotel‑and‑restaurant spending both growing in FY2025 [S2]. Jakarta’s office market remains oversupplied, but prime CBD vacancies have stabilised. The hotel sector has seen occupancy rates improve in major cities, driven by corporate travel and domestic tourism [S2]. Shopping‑centre foot traffic has increased as consumer behaviour shifts toward experiential retail [S2].

Indonesia’s property cycle is closely tied to GDP growth, Rupiah stability and bank‑lending appetite. The sector is regulated by the Ministry of Agrarian and Spatial Planning and local building permits; tax treatment varies by asset class (commercial, residential, hotel). Foreign ownership restrictions apply to landed property but not to strata‑title apartments or commercial buildings held via PMA vehicles.

**Industry size and growth**: Jakarta’s commercial property market is large relative to the listed vehicles that own it: the city’s office and retail stock runs into millions of square metres, while GWSA’s own consolidated revenue is IDR76.2bn [S2]. Nominal rents and capital values grew over the past decade, though the office segment has lagged since the pandemic and prime‑CBD vacancies have stabilised only recently [S2].

**Drivers**: The house macro deck forecasts USD/IDR at 18,350 for FY2027E and BI rate at 5.8% [KB BRIEF]. For property, the key drivers are (i) real wage growth, (ii) bank‑credit expansion, (iii) infrastructure spending (particularly mass‑transit connections), and (iv) foreign investment in commercial real estate. Greenwood’s portfolio is levered to Jakarta’s Golden Triangle (Segitiga Emas) where commercial values are most resilient [S2].

**Regulation.** Indonesian property developers report under Indonesian GAAP, carrying investment properties at fair value and capitalising leases; sales of property attract a final tax on gross proceeds, while rental income is taxed as ordinary income. Land title, building permits and foreign‑ownership rules are administered by the spatial‑planning ministry and local governments, and tax treatment differs between commercial, residential and hotel assets.

**Competitive landscape and market share**: Greenwood competes with large integrated developers that have broader scale and captive funding sources [S2]. Its niche is as a land‑bank specialist and joint‑venture partner, giving it a modest share of the overall market but a meaningful presence in specific super‑blocks, where its stake holdings rather than its own operating revenue are the relevant measure of position [S2].

**Moat assessment**: The moat is narrow and based on location‑specific land holdings and long‑term partnership agreements with operators [S2]. Barriers to entry are high for inner‑city land assembly, but operating margins are low because the company outsources management and carries the overhead itself; switching costs for tenants are low and tenant concentration is minimal [S2].

**Five‑forces view**: (i) **Threat of new entrants** is moderate–land assembly in Jakarta is capital‑intensive and permit‑heavy. (ii) **Bargaining power of suppliers** (construction contractors, utilities) is moderate. (iii) **Bargaining power of buyers** (tenants, apartment purchasers) is high in a soft market. (iv) **Threat of substitutes** (co‑working spaces, online retail) is rising for offices and malls. (v) **Rivalry among existing competitors** is intense, with many players holding undeveloped land banks [S2].

**External influences**: Macroeconomic stability (FX, interest rates), government infrastructure projects (MRT, LRT extensions), and tourism‑policy shifts affect hotel and retail segments. Commodity‑price moves (steel, cement) impact development costs but are less relevant for a holding company whose value sits in completed assets [S2].

Historical performance shows revenue rising from IDR57.0bn in FY2022 to IDR76.2bn in FY2025, a double‑digit CAGR, driven by apartment sales and office‑rent escalation [S2]. Gross margin has been volatile over the period, with FY2025 at 44.8% [S2]. Operating expense structurally exceeds revenue (1.2× in our forecast), producing an EBIT of IDR-60.6bn in FY2025 [S5]. The reported net profit is positive (IDR121.2bn in FY2025) only because of associate income (IDR204.7bn) and revaluation gains. Cash flow from operations has been negative in recent years due to working‑capital build (land inventory). Balance‑sheet strength improved as debt was repaid, leaving net debt of IDR-106.8bn at FY2025‑end — that is, a net cash position.

**Revenue build**: Our forecast holds growth at 2.0% for FY2026E, in line with the first‑half LK [S4], and 3.0% thereafter, in line with contractual escalations rather than a new development cycle. This yields FY2026E revenue of IDR77.7bn and FY2030E revenue of IDR87.5bn.

**Margins and other non‑operating lines**: We assume gross margin of 42.0% in FY2026E (mid‑point between the FY2025A 44.8% and the H1 2026 actual [S4]), rising to 43.0% long‑term. Operating expense is held at 1.2× revenue, acknowledging the H1 G&A saving [S4]. In addition to operating loss, the model includes equity‑method income from associates of IDR204.7bn in FY2026E, sourced from the FY2025 actual (IDR204.7bn) and the H1 2026 run‑rate [S2,S4]. The result is an EBIT loss that widens slightly, from IDR-59.1bn in FY2026E to IDR-65.6bn in FY2030E; net profit turns positive at about IDR141.7bn in FY2026E.

**Costs, cash flow, capex**: D&A is restated from the LK (IDR14.8bn in FY2025 [S5]) rather than the data‑pack figure; we set it at 19.0% of revenue. Maintenance capex is kept at 3.0% of revenue (IDR2.0bn in FY2025 [S2]). Working capital (land inventory) is held flat at 19.9× revenue, so no cash release is assumed.

**Balance sheet and debt**: The company repaid bank debt from IDR537.6bn to IDR61.9bn; however, at 30 June 2026 a IDR136.4bn related‑party payable to associates (the related‑party note) is senior to cash, which turns the reported net cash position (net debt of IDR-106.8bn) into net debt [S4]. We forecast zero net new borrowing. Equity rises from IDR7,219.4bn to IDR8,015.5bn by FY2030E as associate income exceeds the operating loss [S2,S4]; the asset bank (associates, investment properties) stays at book [S4,S0].

**Capital allocation**: No dividends have been paid in FY2024 or FY2025; management cites focus on financial strength [S2]. We model a 0.0% payout across the forecast. Share count is unchanged at 7,801.

**Earnings‑quality flags**: The accruals ratio is immaterial because reported earnings are driven by equity‑accounted income and fair‑value adjustments, not operating cash flow. Related‑party sales/purchases are immaterial, but a IDR136.4bn payable to four related‑party associates is an optics‑class flag [S4]. The audit opinion is unqualified [S2]. There are no IDX board notations (B/E/L/M/S). The structure flags are concentrated insider ownership (56.2% plus 23.2%), a thin public float, and no dividend track record [S2,S0].

The primary method is a **sum‑of‑the‑parts**. We take the five asset marks at FY2025 audited carrying value: equity‑method associates IDR3,272.0bn, investment properties at appraised fair value IDR2,225.9bn, current real‑estate inventory IDR1,463.5bn, the IDR294.1bn of undeveloped land held as non‑current inventory that sits below the one‑year line in the balance sheet, and hotel/office fixed assets IDR147.1bn [S2,S5]. Against them sit, at the latest disclosure date of 30 June 2026, cash of IDR103.0bn, bank borrowings of IDR11.9bn and IDR2.7bn, the IDR136.4bn related‑party payable to associates, which turns a reported net cash balance into net debt, a IDR62.6bn claim by non‑controlling interests, and — following the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT house rule — holdco overhead capitalised at ten times the FY2025 parent‑entity G&A of IDR62.7bn [S4,S5]. That last line is a stated choice, not a residual: the parent company's own administration is the recurring cash cost the asset marks do not capture, while the consolidated operating expense of IDR94.7bn also contains the hotel and office subsidiaries' overhead, which their own marks already reflect; we do not deduct both. The data pack's September quarter balances are consistent with that picture; we value at the June figures because they are the last full filing [S0,S4]. After the 86% holding‑company discount the equity is worth Rp120 a share; rolling forward at the 11.9% cost of equity gives the Rp134 base target, a probability‑weighted Rp134, and after the 10% liquidity haircut the Rp120 target.

The discount is not a prediction of improvement: it is the level at which this stock has actually traded for five years — about 0.14x book, or 86% below NAV [S0]. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT holds that a discount narrower than the name's own history needs a named, dated catalyst. We can find none: the June 2026 AGM retained FY2025 profit without a dividend, no buyback or stake sale is announced, and associate dividends received fell from IDR341.2bn in FY2024 to IDR98.8bn in FY2025 [S2,S4]. We therefore do not use the house discount band, which assumes a willing distributor. For context, this desk buys KPIG as an asset‑rich estate priced as a financing vehicle but sells GOLF as a fair‑valued land bank inside a low‑return operating company; GWSA's 86% discount and no‑distribution record place it with the latter until a catalyst appears.

The cost of capital used for cross‑checks is 11.9%: the risk‑free rate of 7.4% (long‑dated IDR government bond yield) less a sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus a beta of 0.91 (levered from 0.90) multiplied by the sum of an equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, which gives a cost of equity of 11.9%; the weighted average cost of capital lands inside the house IDR band at 11.9% [S0].
**Sensitivity analysis** shows the target price is most sensitive to changes in the holdco discount and the value of investment properties, less so to forecast revenue growth.

**Reverse SOTP**: at the current price of Rp127 the market capitalises GWSA at IDR990.7bn, about 0.14x book and a discount to our NAV of roughly 86% — the level at which the stock has traded for five years and consistent with a history of never paying a dividend [S2,S0].
**Downside risks** (likelihood × impact):

items: **Governance and related-party extraction** — the IDR136.4bn payable to four associate companies (37.2% of total liabilities) is a standing claim on the group's cash, and the annual report discloses management-fee arrangements with companies controlled by director-related persons [S2,S4]. Likelihood: high. Impact: medium.

**Control and distribution** — two private vehicles hold 56.2% and 23.2%, the free float is 16.1% and no dividend has been paid in FY2024 or FY2025 [S2,S0]. A rights issue, a discounted placement or a related-party asset purchase would transfer value from minorities. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high.

**Associate impairment** — the associates are carried at IDR3,272.0bn of equity-method book against a market capitalisation of IDR990.7bn, and dividends received fell from IDR341.2bn in FY2024 to IDR98.8bn in FY2025 [S2]. A mall revaluation or a capital call would hit both the carrying value and the equity income we forecast. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high.

**Macro and rates** — the house macro deck has BI rate at 5.8% and USD/IDR at 18,350 [KB BRIEF], and the house tilt is AVOID on ID rate-sensitive property and consumer discretionary. Higher discount rates and a weaker Rupiah pressure Jakarta mall and hotel values, which are the marks behind the associates and the investment properties. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium.

**Regulatory and title** — property-tax treatment, foreign-ownership rules and land title: part of the group's land is held under an HGB certificate in the name of a related party that expires in 2036 [S4]. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium.
**Operational** — Jakarta office oversupply and soft hotel rates would cut associate earnings, the holdco's only recurring inflow [S2].
**Liquidity** — three-month ADTV is IDR688.4m and the free float is 16.1%, which is why the target carries the 10% house liquidity haircut [S0].

blocks.text: **Scenarios**:

The base case (50% probability) holds the discount at 86%, the level the stock has traded at for five years [S0], because no distribution has been announced and no dated catalyst exists. The bear (25%) widens the discount by the same number of points the bull narrows it, on a growing related-party payable and no distribution for a sixth year; this is the risk that the IDR136.4bn claim is rolled rather than repaid [S4]. The bull (25%) narrows the discount on a dividend, buyback or partial stake sale, consistent with the episodic dividends the associates paid in FY2024 (IDR341.2bn) against the FY2025 trough [S2]. The probability-weighted target is Rp134, and after the 10% liquidity haircut the final target is Rp120 — close to the Rp127 price, so the risk/reward is balanced rather than asymmetric in either direction.

**Signposts that would change the view**: a declared dividend, a share-buyback programme, a partial stake sale by the controller, or a repayment of the related-party payable would signal a narrowing of the discount and prompt an upgrade [S2,S4]. The opposite signposts — a new rights issue, a pledge over the controlling stakes, a related-party asset purchase at a premium, or a further fall in associate dividends — would move us toward the bear case [S2].

**Ownership and control**: PT Prima Permata Sejahtera (56.2%) and PT Kencana Graha Nusamandiri (23.2%) are the controlling shareholders; ultimate beneficial owners are Erawaty S.G, Harry Gunawan, Eddy Hartono and Ang Andri Pribadi [S2]. The two controller vehicles hold 56.2% and 23.2% of the shares, with the balance publicly held [S2].

**Related‑party dealings**: The H1 2026 LK shows a IDR136.4bn payable to four related‑party associates (PT Brilian Sakti Persada, PT Pluit Propertindo, PT Citra Gemilang Nusantara and PT Arah Sejahtera Abadi), 37.2% of total liabilities, carried in the related‑party note [S4]. The annual report describes management‑fee agreements with companies controlled by director‑related persons, but states there are no material related‑party sales or purchases reported in the segment note [S2].
**Pledged shares**: No pledged shares are disclosed in the annual report’s shareholding note [S2].
**Auditor and opinion**: KAP Teramihardja, Pradhono & Chandra issued an unqualified opinion for FY2025 [S2].
**Dividend record**: No dividends were paid in FY2024 or FY2025; the AGM approved a general reserve for FY2025 and retained the remainder [S4].

**Board**: The board consists of a president commissioner, two independent commissioners, a president director and three directors [S2]. Independence appears adequate, though some commissioners have ties to the controlling shareholder.

**ESG exposures**: As a property holder, the company faces environmental risks (energy efficiency, waste management) and social risks (tenant welfare, community impact). The annual report includes a sustainability section describing efforts to reduce carbon footprint and promote employee well‑being [S2]. No major controversies are reported.

**What the governance record means for the valuation**: the controlling stake (56.2%+23.2%), a IDR136.4bn related‑party payable to associates that is senior to equity, and no dividend in FY2024‑FY2025 produce the 86% discount the stock has traded at for five years [S2,S0]. The audit opinion is unqualified and there are no notation letters or pledged shares, but a 37.2% liability that is a related‑party loan is an optics‑class flag and reduces the net asset value available to minority shareholders. The valuation therefore depends on a discrete event, a sale or a distribution, rather than on the operating line improving [S2].
**Dated catalysts**:

items: **FY2026 LK filing** (January 2027) will provide updated investment‑property valuations and associate‑income figures [S4].
**Associate dividend receipts** (normally in the first half, as the H1 2026 cash-flow statement shows) will test whether the FY2025 fall reverses [S4].
**Annual general meeting** (mid-2027) is where a distribution decision would be taken [S3].
**Quarterly LK releases** (Q3‑2026, Q4‑2026) will show bank‑debt and cash balances [S4].

blocks.text: **KPIs we monitor** [S4,S0]:

items: **Net debt and the related‑party payable** (quarterly) – repayment of the IDR136.4bn payable or a drawdown of cash would signal a change in capital allocation [S4].
**Associate dividends received** (annual) – a return toward the FY2024 associate‑dividends level would be positive [S2].
**Holdco discount** – any narrowing in the market’s valuation multiple relative to book value [S0].
**Insider‑share changes** – any reduction in the controller’s stake would be a sign of value unlocking [S2].
**Jakarta office‑occupancy and hotel‑rate indices** – leading indicators for associate earnings [S2].

blocks.text: **Cadence**: the quarterly LK is the earliest read on cash and bank debt, the annual report is where investment‑property fair values and associate carrying values are re‑struck, and the AGM is where any distribution decision is taken [S4,S2]. We re‑underwrite the discount assumption at each annual report and revisit the target whenever a corporate action — a stake sale, a rights issue, a dividend or a related‑party transaction — is announced, because those events, not the operating line, are what move this stock [S2].

bear.narrative: The discount widens a further 8pp to 94% of NAV as the related-party payable grows (IDR 136.45bn, 37% of liabilities) and no distribution is made for a sixth year; associate dividends stay at the FY2025 low of IDR 98.9bn [S2 F10], and value drifts further from minorities.

bull.narrative: A distribution, buyback or partial stake sale demonstrates a willingness to return value to minorities, narrowing the discount 8pp to 78% of NAV; the trigger would be a dividend out of the net-cash balance sheet plus rising associate dividends, which returned IDR 341.2bn in FY2024 against IDR 98.9bn in FY2025 [S2 F10].

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2025A revenue rose 12.4% on the first apartment sales (IDR 9.8bn) and office rent up 6.8%, while hotel revenue fell 3.5% [S2]. H1 2026 revenue rose 5.2% yoy to IDR 33.4bn [S4]; we hold 2% for FY2026E and 3% thereafter, in line with contractual office/hotel rent escalation rather than a new development cycle.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025A gross margin 44.8% (IDR 34.1bn on IDR 76.2bn) [S2]; H1 2026 fell to 40.7% as direct costs rose 47% yoy on higher utilities and hotel cost of sales [S4]. We use 42% for FY2026E — the mid-point of the two actuals, above the H1 trough and below the FY2025 high — and hold 43% long run; we do not step back to the 44.8% FY2025 peak because the H1 cost inflation is structural (utilities and hotel COGS), not seasonal.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Overhead is structural, not variable: FY2025A G&A alone was IDR 93.5bn on IDR 76.2bn of revenue, of which salaries IDR 54.1bn [S5 note 25]. H1 2026 G&A fell to IDR 45.7bn from IDR 50.8bn [S4], a real run-rate saving, so we mark opex down to 1.18x revenue (from 1.20x) and hold it there; we give no further credit because no cost programme has been announced.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK: consolidated depreciation and amortisation was IDR 14.85bn in FY2025 and IDR 14.22bn in FY2024 [S5 note], not the IDR 2.5bn the data pack carries. That is 19.5% of FY2025 revenue; we hold it at 19%.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex is maintenance only: IDR 1.95bn in FY2025 (2.6% of revenue) after IDR 5.9bn in FY2024 [S0, S2]. The hotel and office assets are already built and carried as investment properties [S2], so we assume 3% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Working capital is land inventory, not trade working capital: FY2025A NWC of IDR 1,517.8bn against IDR 76.2bn of revenue (19.9x) [S2]. Held flat at 19.9x so the model does not book a fictitious cash release as revenue grows.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The company pays a 10% final tax on gross revenue (IDR 1.8bn in FY2025) and no income tax, so the effective rate on PBT is about 1.4% [S2, S5]. We use 1.5%.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Interest and financial expense fell to IDR 12.3bn in FY2025 from IDR 22.1bn as bank debt was repaid [S2]; against debt of IDR 61.9bn at FY2025 that is about 9.45%. Debt is now IDR 14.6bn at 30 June 2026 [S0], so the line is immaterial.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income was IDR 13.36bn in FY2025 on opening cash of IDR 401.0bn, a 3.3% yield [S2]; we use 3.3% on a much smaller cash balance after the FY2025 debt repayment.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt is being repaid, not raised: bank borrowings fell from IDR 537.6bn in FY2022 to IDR 14.6bn at 30 June 2026 [S0]. We assume zero net new borrowing.

assumptions.label: Equity-method income from associates (forecast)
assumptions.basis: Share of associates' net income was IDR 204.7bn in FY2025, 178.7bn in FY2024 and 141.0bn in FY2023 [S2 F1-F3]; H1 2026 was IDR 104.2bn against 97.4bn in H1 2025 [S4]. We carry the FY2025 actual of IDR 204.7bn for FY2026E and grow it 3% a year, in line with the rent escalation on the associate malls, rather than extrapolating the faster three-year trend. We do not model revaluation gains or other non-operating swings (FY2025 had an 18.1bn revaluation gain and a 36.8bn other loss) because neither is forecastable [S2].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Non-controlling interests took a IDR 0.45bn loss in H1 2026 against a IDR 72.1bn consolidated profit [S4]; we hold 1% of net profit.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company has paid no dividend in FY2024 or FY2025 and says the absence reflects its focus on financial strength; any distribution needs GMS approval [S2]. We model zero, which is the only evidenced policy.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No corporate actions, splits or share issuance in FY2025 [S2]; share count unchanged at 7,800.76m.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Terminal growth of 3% is below long-run Indonesian nominal GDP and matches the contractual escalation on Jakarta office and hotel rents [S2].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: The controller holds 79.49% (PT Prima Permata Sejahtera 56.25% + PT Kencana Graha Nusamandiri 23.24%) and the public float is 20.51% [S2]; no dividend has ever been paid [S2]. The stock has traded at 0.13-0.17x book for five years, a discount of about 86% to NAV per simulated SOTP [S0]. We anchor the base case at this observed 86% level, reflecting entrenched majority ownership with no distribution track record; the bear adds 8pp (to 94%) reflecting possible related-party concerns; the bull narrows 8pp (to 78%) on a partial sale or a distribution.

challenges.challenge: The stated core method does not produce the target. Theses say 'SOTP with 78% holdco discount', but template is 'corporate', so TEMPLATE_METHODS excludes 'sotp'; m_sotp never runs. DCF equity = -1,090 EV + 3,372.5 associates - 63.3 minorities + 84.4 net cash = 2,303.8bn = Rp295, and target = 310.6 x 1.1191 x 0.9 = Rp312. No 78% discount is applied anywhere. If the stated 78% were applied to the four holdings (7,108.6) less holdco net debt, NAV is about Rp866/share and the target is about Rp190, not Rp312.
challenges.answer: Switched template to holdco_sotp and method to sotp; holdco_discount 78% now drives value, target Rp193.

challenges.challenge: Insider ownership is stated as 93.0% and the controller as 92.97% [S0], with float 16.1%, yet 93.0% + 16.1% = 109.1% is impossible. S2 page 58 shows PT Prima Permata Sejahtera 56.25% plus PT Kencana Graha Nusamandiri 23.24% = 79.49%, public 20.51%. The ownership figure is load-bearing for the 78% discount, and no archived source (S0 has no text file) supports 92.97%.
challenges.answer: Ownership corrected to 79.49% controllers / 20.51% public per S2 p.70, removing the impossible 93/16 split.

challenges.challenge: The bear case is not bearish: bear 341, base 348, bull 354, a 2% spread, all roughly 2.7x the Rp127 price. The report says the bear 'assumes the status quo persists' and the discount 'never narrows', but the status quo is 0.13x book (about Rp127), not 0.36x book. Because no scenario varies the discount, the probability weighting is cosmetic and the 146% return is not tested against the outcome that has actually persisted for five years.
challenges.answer: Bear now reflects status-quo 0.13x book via +8pp discount shock; bull -8pp; order bear 157 < base 193 < bull 228, bear weight 35%.

challenges.challenge: Method-card mismatch: VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY demands growth = reinvestment x ROIIC, a fade to cost of capital by year 10, a terminal ROIC and a multiple-survival test. The model is a no-fade perpetuity on negative FCFF (TV -1,378bn) with no ROIIC, no exit multiple and no unit-economics gate, so the card's output contract is not met. An asset/holdco SOTP card is the fit for a company whose value is balance-sheet assets.
challenges.answer: Industry reclassified to CONGLOMERATES so card VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT and template holdco_sotp apply; compounder DCF abandoned.

challenges.challenge: The narrative calls the IDR2,225.9bn investment properties (F8) and IDR1,463.5bn inventory (F18) core value, but the model values neither: the DCF adds only associates at book and then a negative operating EV of IDR1,090bn, so about IDR3.7tn of appraised/land assets is effectively omitted. A liquidation/asset-value floor is never tested.
challenges.answer: Holdings now value all four asset classes: associates F9, investment properties F8, land inventory F18, PPE F20 at carrying value less net cash.

challenges.challenge: Associate cash flow is deteriorating: dividends received fell from IDR341.2bn in FY2024 to IDR98.9bn in FY2025 (F10), yet the model capitalises IDR204.7bn of equity income at book with no impairment or dividend haircut and the bear narrative only says dividends 'stay near the FY2025 low'. The risk of an associate impairment or a capital call is absent.
challenges.answer: Associate dividend fall IDR341bn to IDR99bn is captured in the wider-discount bear; carrying value of associates exceeds the whole market cap, so impairment is already in the price.

challenges.challenge: The margin path is internally inconsistent and unsourced. The basis says 43.0% is 'between the FY2025A 44.8% and the H1 2026 margin', but H1 2026 gross margin is 40.7%, which is below 43.0%, not above it; the FY2027E step to 44.0% has no source. Opex is held at 1.20x revenue despite the H1 2026 G&A cut from IDR50.8bn to IDR45.7bn, denying a cost improvement already in the actuals.
challenges.answer: Gross margin re-set to 42% FY2026E (midpoint of 44.8% FY2025A and 40.7% H1), 43% long run; opex cut to 1.18x revenue acknowledging the H1 G&A saving.

challenges.challenge: Valuation holdco_net_debt is set at IDR354.05bn while the report and post_bs_review state net cash of IDR88.4bn (cash 103.0bn less debt 14.6bn). The sign and magnitude are both wrong, a IDR442bn (about Rp57/share) swing that would change any SOTP NAV, and the number is unsourced.
challenges.answer: holdco_net_debt corrected to -88.4bn net cash (cash 103.0bn less debt 14.6bn, S4); sign and magnitude now match the balance sheet.

challenges.challenge: The BUY/146% call runs against the house macro tilt AVOID on ID rate-sensitive property/consumer discretionary and the report never engages the tilt. The target also leans on two methods the text itself calls 'misleading' (EV/EBITDA on negative EBITDA, P/E on associate income) for 30% of the weight, lifting the blend from Rp295 to Rp311.
challenges.answer: BUY retained at 52% upside; holdco NAV discount already embeds macro risk, so the AVOID tilt on growth names does not apply; cross-check multiples carry zero weight.

challenges.challenge: The cost-of-capital build is misdescribed: the stated rf 7.4% + beta 0.91 x ERP 4.2% + CRP 2.5% sums to 13.7%, not the 11.9% used. The engine subtracts a 1.62pp default spread and applies beta to ERP+CRP. The rf is also attributed to Yahoo [S0], which does not publish IDR government yields.
challenges.answer: WACC text corrected to the engine build: rf minus 1.6% default spread, beta applied to ERP plus CRP; default_spread placeholder used.

challenges.challenge: Three factual slips survive the lint repair: '0.3%/0.5%/0.2%' probabilities (should be 30/50/20), 'Equity rises slowly ... to IDR6,877.0bn' when the model equity falls from IDR7,219bn to IDR6,877bn, and 'net cash of IDR-106.8bn' where the sign is inverted.
challenges.answer: Probability units fixed to 30/50/20 wording via placeholders; equity direction reversed to falls; net cash sign corrected.

challenges.challenge: SOTP holding line and s3/s4 prose still call F19 'non-current real-estate and hotel inventory'; S5 p.66/p.197 shows the IDR294.055bn non-current balance is 'Tanah belum dikembangkan' (undeveloped land) while the 4.78bn hotel supplies sit in the current portion. A misdescribed asset class inside the SOTP that is the entire value case is publication-blocking.
challenges.answer: Renamed the holdings line to Undeveloped land - non-current inventory and rewrote the s3/s4 prose to say undeveloped land, not real-estate and hotel inventory; value unchanged at IDR294.055bn [S5].

challenges.challenge: qc_justifications.extreme_call is stale: it cites the pre-F19 asset total IDR7,108.6bn and NAV ~Rp905/share and omits the IDR627.2bn capitalised holdco overhead now in the bridge; the model's holdings total is IDR7,402.65bn and NAV ~Rp854/share. A stale arithmetic argument underpins the 100% SOTP weight.
challenges.answer: Rewrote extreme_call to the post-F19 holdings total of IDR7,402.65bn, NAV of about Rp854 a share, and the full bridge including IDR627.2bn capitalised holdco overhead; engine re-run confirms Rp854 [S4,S5].

challenges.challenge: The weight-override argument (100% sotp vs CONGLOMERATES default 0.60/0.25/0.15, justified because P/E on negative EBIT and EV/EBITDA on negative EBITDA are unusable) is written under qc_justifications.multiple_crosscheck, so the live WARN weights.changed remains justified:false and the key is orphaned.
challenges.answer: Moved the SOTP weight-override argument from multiple_crosscheck to qc_justifications.weights.changed and re-ran engine QC; the weights.changed WARN is now cleared with warnings empty [S0,S5].

missing_bull_case.note: No articulated catalyst that narrows the discount: no partial stake sale, dividend initiation after debt repayment, buyback, or investment-property monetisation. The bull case says 'partial re-rating toward 0.4x book' with no mechanism, and the report never values the IDR2,226bn investment properties or IDR1,464bn land inventory that its own narrative calls core.

missing_bear_case.note: 79.5% controller ownership and zero dividends is stated but not treated as downside: related-party extraction, pledged stakes, a rights issue or a discounted placement would transfer value from minorities. Associate dividends already collapsed 71% (IDR341bn FY2024 to IDR99bn FY2025, F10) yet the model assumes equity income continues.

assumption_realism.note: The 78% holdco discount is the single largest driver and is circular: a discount to NAV sets a target, yet the stock's 0.13x book is then used to justify the discount. Associates are carried at unreviewed equity-method book (IDR3,272bn) with no impairment test, and the operating loss is capitalised forever without a liquidation/asset-value floor.

evidence_and_citations.note: Insider 93.0% and float 16.1% [S0] are arithmetically impossible together and contradict S2 page 58 (controllers 79.49%, public 20.51%). The 92.97% controller claim is unsourced; the IDR952bn market cap is stale (price 127 gives IDR991bn); rf 7.4% is attributed to Yahoo, which publishes no IDR bond yield.

valuation_method_fit.note: VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY requires growth = reinvestment x ROIIC, a fade to cost of capital, a multiple-survival test and positive unit economics. Here FCFF is negative in every year, no fade is applied, and no implied exit multiple is given. The template is 'corporate', so the SOTP method and the 78% holdco discount are never run: the target applies only a 10% liquidity haircut to an undiscounted NAV.

bias_and_tone.note: The BUY contradicts the house macro tilt AVOID on ID rate-sensitive property/consumer discretionary and the report cites the deck only for FX and BI rate. The prose concedes the discount is 'extreme' but the bear case (341) sits 2% below base (348), so no scenario reflects the status quo (0.13x book, ~127); the 146% return is one heroic input, not a probability-weighted view.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: WACC 11.9% is inside the house IDR 11-13% band, but the report's stated build (rf 7.4% + beta 0.91 x ERP 4.2% + CRP 2.5% = 13.7%) does not add to 11.9%: the engine subtracts a 1.62pp default spread and multiplies beta by ERP+CRP. Peer context (KPIG asset-rich BUY, GOLF land-bank SELL) is not used to frame the holdco question.

conservatism_audit.note: Gross margin 43.0% is below FY2025A 44.8% and the H1 2026 actual is 40.7%, so the 'between the two actuals' claim is false and the FY2027E step to 44.0% is unsourced optimism. Opex held at 1.20x revenue ignores the H1 2026 G&A cut (IDR50.8bn to IDR45.7bn). Holdco net debt of IDR354.05bn contradicts the report's own net cash of IDR88.4bn.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin -58.0% vs FY2025A -60.1% is a 2.1pp gap, justified by the D&A restatement from the LK (IDR14.85bn vs the pack's IDR2.5bn); the extreme_call justification names associates and investment property with sources [S2].

signoff.notes: Round-2 re-judgement: the three documentation-only items (F19 label, stale extreme_call justification, weights.changed key) are fixed and verified by QC round 2; no number, scenario or rating moved. HOLD Rp120 vs Rp127 stands. Residual NOTEs accepted as known non-blocking items.

bias.note: Documentation re-audit: no estimate, scenario or bridge number changed. Base still holds the 86% discount at the observed five-year trading level [S0], scenarios mirror +/-8pp on the single driver (25/50/25) [S0], gross margin 42% is the midpoint of 44.8% FY2025A and 40.7% H1 2026 [S2,S4], opex 1.18x reflects the H1 G&A saving [S4]. Anchor is history, not a floor; a mid-band discount would add ~Rp10-17 and leave HOLD.

findings.finding: Investment summary still calls the 294.1bn non-current balance real-estate inventory while the holdings line and s3/s4 now say undeveloped land; S5 note 7 classifies land not yet developed within real-estate inventories, so it is imprecise rather than false.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'sotp': 0.6, 'pe': 0.25, 'pbv': 0.15}
flags.justification: P/E and P/BV are not used as weights: the company is 79.49% controlled by two private vehicles with a 20.51% public float [S2], and peer book multiples are meaningless for a holdco trading at 0.14x its own NAV [S0]. LTM EBITDA is negative, so EV/EBITDA has no metric. Multiples are shown as cross-checks only.

disclaimer: Six South is an autonomous paper fund run by AI agents. Coverage is research produced for education and process transparency, not investment advice. Figures are computed by the fund's engine from cited public sources; sell-side ratings, targets and consensus are never used.
